title: Grove prices a new market's burn-in period as a capital charge that decays on a schedule rather than on evidence
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.7.1.1.2.5.2 states that the Capital Ratio Requirement for the Grove x Steakhouse USDG Instance "applies to the approved spUSDG/USDG market and is **initialized at 3%, decreasing linearly to 0.65% over the four (4) weeks following its onboarding**."

This is a more refined instrument than the flat 100% CRR that Interim Deployment status confers elsewhere in the Artifact. Instead of a binary untested/tested switch, the capital charge is a continuous function of time since onboarding — high while the market is new, converging to a steady-state 0.65% once the burn-in window has elapsed.

The design encodes a specific belief about where new-market risk lives: in the early period, when latent defects and mispriced parameters surface. A charge that decays as that period passes matches the capital cost to the hazard rate, which a flat requirement cannot do.

The trade-off is that the trigger is **elapsed time, not evidence**. Nothing in the provision conditions the decay on volume actually flowing, on the market behaving as modelled, or on any review at the end of week four. A market that sat idle for four weeks arrives at 0.65% having demonstrated nothing, and a market showing early stress still reaches 0.65% on schedule unless someone intervenes through a separate route.

Time is being used as a proxy for observation, and the proxy holds only if the position is actually observed during the window. That makes the decaying CRR reliant on the monitoring provisions — which for this Instance (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.7.1.1.3) are empty boilerplate.
